clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man with a history of Roux-en-Y bypass surgery presented with severe diarrhea, significant weight loss, and steatorrhea. Diagnostic workup revealed a very low fecal elastase level (<40 μg/g) and massive steatorrhea (277 g/24h). His symptoms, including diarrhea and weight loss, significantly improved within 2 months of initiating pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with clinical symptoms consistent with malabsorption and EPI, including severe diarrhea, 41-kg weight loss, progressive muscle weakness, recurrent falls, oily/greasy stools, and excessive foul-smelling gas.
Patient had a history of Roux-en-Y bypass surgery 35 years prior, a risk factor for EPI.
Fecal elastase level was less than 40 μg/g, indicating severe exocrine pancreatic insufficiency.
A 48-hour fecal fat study demonstrated massive steatorrhea (total fat in 24 hours of 277 g).
Diarrhea and weight loss improved significantly 2 months after initiation of pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT).

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Patient's known prior history explicitly states no acute or chronic pancreatitis.
